paragraphs: Rav Menashe, Rav Yehudah's student, first chapter of Ḥullin 4a. Mnemonic: 'brings in, knife, with males.' Tosafot writes that it is a mnemonic for Rav Menashe's teachings: here, 'he brings them under his wings'; in chapter 2(31a), R. Menashe says, 'with a knife without horns,' and Rav Aḥa son of Rav Avya spoke to him; there 51a, R. Menasya says, 'These rams of thieves.' Yevamot 2(25): R. Menashe says, 'A robber by rabbinic law'; Mi SheHeḥshikh 156; Kelal Gadol 74b: R. Menashe said. Avodah Zarah 26a: Rav Menashi met thieves, who said, 'You are a student of the Yehudai'; Rashi explains, Rav Yehudah's student. Shabbat 145a: the house of Menashe taught—I am uncertain whether this is another figure, since 'taught' is used of him as of a baraita; see the general rules and Rabbi above—that by Torah law liability applies only to treading olives and grapes, and testimony relayed by a witness is valid only for a woman's marital-status testimony. 'The house of Menashe taught,' Eruvin 95b, 97b; Yoma 77b; Bekhorot 36b. R. Assi said to Rav Ashi (the early one), 'But R. Menashe taught.' Rav Assi was Rav's student-colleague; how could he speak in Rav Yehudah's student's name? Thus this figure appears earlier than Rav Yehudah. Perhaps Rav Menashi was Rav Yehudah's student, while Rav Menashe was not.
